purpose: Adversarial corner-case and interrogatory framework for the Graphable, Enrichable, Verifiable system. It gives deterministic and LLM/human reviewers reusable question sets, skill templates, and challenge cases so review packets maximize context and minimize confusion, hidden blast radius, and unsupported fixes.

corner_case_categories.review_goal: Mark unresolved references explicitly and block automatic rename or promotion until modeled.
Use shims or explicit exemptions for external names while keeping typed internal implementations.
Rename code and serialized/public field surfaces only as a coordinated contract.

risks: scalar config where array/map is needed
corner_case_categories.review_goal: Prefer scalar-or-sequence normalization, maps, dispatch tables, and bounded iteration primitives.
Make flow graphable, bounded, and rule/table driven where cases can grow.
Expose side effects, idempotency keys, rollback paths, receipts, and proof fixtures.
Attach import/export/caller/UI path context before changing a symbol.
Route to high-risk review and require deterministic evidence plus owner/human acceptance.
Use explicit timestamps, injected clocks, freshness policies, and stale-holdout behavior.
Keep meaningful names but use shims, summaries, aliases, and generated graph views when names hit external limits.
Represent frontend-to-backend seams as graph paths and mark missing parser coverage as a gap.
Use Teleon primitive blocks, candidate envelopes, purpose/input/output contracts, and proof-before-promotion.

questions: What node(s) does this artifact create or modify?
What edge types should exist: calls, contains, imports, data_def_use, UI seam, requirement edge?
What dynamic or unresolved edge could hide from static parsing?
Can this be found by exact grep using the long source name?
Who calls this, imports this, re-exports this, or serializes this?
Which UI/backend paths reach it?
Which proofs fail if this changes?
What is the smallest bounded slice that can be safely migrated?
What purpose does this object serve?
What problem does it solve?
What inputs and outputs does it expect today?
What UI/UX or product behavior depends on it?
What would confuse an LLM or engineer reading only this packet?
Which deterministic check proves the finding exists?
Which proof or test accepts a fix?
What nondeterministic enrichment is merely candidate-only?
What human/owner review is required before promotion?
Is this scalar actually one element of a repeated set?
Should input be scalar_or_sequence instead of scalar-only?
Can a table, array, map, or dispatch row replace this branch or repeated call?
What Teleon primitive block would make the shape scalable?
What name, field, method, or module is being resolved dynamically?
Can the possible targets be enumerated into a dispatch table?
Does this block automatic rename or data-flow confidence?
What fixture proves each dynamic target remains reachable?
Is this a real secret, a fixture, or a detector pattern?
Is the value synthetic and clearly marked?
Can the pattern leak into docs, logs, prompts, or deployed artifacts?
Which redaction or fixture-marker proof should guard it?
Is this name called by a framework, CLI, template, or external user?
Should it remain as a shim while the implementation gets the long pyprefix name?
Which callers use keyword names, string names, route names, or serialized keys?
What compatibility proof prevents breaking public behavior?

skill_templates.role: Map nodes and edges before proposing fixes.
skill_templates.prompt_frame: List the graph nodes, edge types, unresolved edges, and blast-radius level for this packet. Do not propose a fix until the blast radius is named.

skill_templates.role: Find public/API/schema/framework contracts that a rename or refactor could break.
skill_templates.prompt_frame: Assume this change breaks an external contract. Name the contract, evidence, and shim or coordinated migration required.

skill_templates.role: Find scalar-to-array, loop, dispatch, and rule-table opportunities.
skill_templates.prompt_frame: Identify whether the code should become scalar_or_sequence, table-driven, dispatch-driven, or bounded-loop driven. Name the primitive block.
State the deterministic evidence, proof command, required fixture, and why LLM output alone is insufficient.

skill_templates.role: Imagine ways the finding or fix fails under dynamic, concurrent, malformed, stale, or cross-tenant inputs.
skill_templates.prompt_frame: Generate adversarial cases, including dynamic refs, malformed input, repeated input, stale facts, tenant boundaries, and public contract callers.

skill_templates.role: Map code risk to UI, user workflow, and product-market behavior.
skill_templates.prompt_frame: Explain the UX/product impact if this code is wrong, stale, unwired, or confusing. Keep claims candidate-only.
